executive_summary: A heavyweight Premier League weekend is dominated by Arsenal's title charge at a down-form Newcastle, while the Championship serves up an unmissable top-of-the-table collision between Stoke and Birmingham, both on 29 points. Four matches clear the 0.80 singles threshold — Wolves, Middlesbrough, Tottenham and Bournemouth all carry compelling home-advantage cases — but the Crystal Palace new-manager bounce under Thomas Frank and the injury carnage across both Bolton and Portsmouth make games 6, 7 and 8 genuine coupons for the bin if caution is required.
value_radar: Game 10 (Sheffield vs Watford): Watford's away record is catastrophically bad (W0 D1 L6, one point from 7 away games) and Sheffield are UP-FORM with dominant H2H — yet the odds of 1.66 may actually understate how likely a home win is given Watford's structural inability to pick up road points.

Game 12 (Swansea vs West Brom): West Brom at 2.80 looks generous given Swansea's triple injury/suspension crisis (Ronald, Franco, Stamenic all out) combined with an interim coaching panel who have had two training sessions together. West Brom's xGF of 2.89 in the last five games is the highest number on this coupon.

Game 6 (Coventry vs Crystal Palace): Thomas Frank's new-manager bounce is a real variable but Palace's most dangerous attackers — Mateta (suspended) and Sarr (out) — are both unavailable for his debut. Coventry's 2.48 may be slight value given they face a structurally weakened Palace side.

predictions.analysis:
Arsenal arrive at St James' Park as the Premier League's form team, sitting top of the table and carrying a five-game winning sequence in all competitions until they were held by Fleetwood in the EFL Cup — a game they clearly did not care about. Their away record of W4 D0 L1 this season, with the solitary loss inflated by a cup rotation, is the second-best in the division, and their xGA of 0.76 per game is a defensive statement. The concern, and it is a real one, is Bukayo Saka. His quadriceps injury, confirmed by Arteta as ruling him out until at least late December, removes Arsenal's most direct threat, their most reliable set-piece delivery and their top scorer in a single blow. That said, Arsenal beat Liverpool away from home without him, and the evidence of their last five xG numbers — 1.70 xGF against 0.88 xGA — suggests the system is bigger than any individual.

Newcastle, by contrast, carry every hallmark of a team under internal pressure. The DOWN-FORM flag is deserved: they have won once in their last five Premier League matches, their home record of W1 D2 L2 ranks 17th in the division, and they concede an xGA of 1.67 per game. Their underlying defensive numbers are fragile — a team ranked 17th at home cannot rely on structure to protect them against an Arsenal side generating nearly five shots on target per game. Joelinton's absence matters in terms of physicality and energy in the press, though Miley and Ramsey are capable deputies.

The head-to-head record underlines Arsenal's dominance. They have won three of the last four league meetings, with the only Newcastle win coming in a two-legged EFL Cup tie two seasons ago. This is a fixture Arsenal have been winning in the league with increasing authority. The 1.6 odds represent a very heavy favourite status that the market has priced correctly — the public backing of 62% is not irrational here, though the absence of Saka introduces genuine variability in chance creation.

The prediction is an Arsenal away win. They have the squad depth, the system and the motivation of a title charge. Newcastle at home in this form are a beatable side, and the xG data confirms Arsenal's defensive solidity is real rather than lucky — their xPts of 20 almost perfectly matches their actual 27 points, suggesting the table flatters them only marginally. Arsenal win, though the absence of Saka keeps confidence shy of a high-singles threshold.
predictions.value_note: Arsenal at 1.6 is a correctly priced heavy favourite. No overlay, but the prediction is clear.

predictions.analysis:
This is the most injury-distorted match in the Premier League section of the coupon. Chelsea arrive at this fixture missing five confirmed players, a list that would concern any manager: top scorer João Pedro (5G/3A) is out, Reece James — their primary set-piece delivery specialist — is sidelined, and two first-choice defenders in Lacroix and Hato are unavailable alongside winger Gittens. Xabi Alonso must therefore construct an attack around Pedro Neto without his most reliable striker, and a defence that has conceded 1.5 goals per game by xGA this season facing reshaping at the back.

Yet the counter-argument is powerful. Leeds away from home have been mediocre: W1 D2 L2 on the road this season, with a goal difference of minus-two in those five games. Their xGF of 1.09 and xGA of 1.22 in the last five games describe a team that neither creates nor concedes heavily — a mid-table Championship-level away performance, essentially. And the most important piece of context is the EFL Cup meeting earlier this season: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds at Stamford Bridge. That was a cup game, perhaps not fully representative, but it demonstrated the talent differential between these two squads even in a more experimental Chelsea setup.

Leeds' manager Daniel Farke has described Chelsea as a side with world-class potential, which reads as a team setting up not to lose rather than to win. With Anton Stach and Noah Okafor both doubtful on Perplexity's report (unverified by structured data), Leeds may also be short of creativity in midfield. The structured source confirms only Mateo Joseph as confirmed out for Leeds, so their situation is better than Chelsea's numerically.

This remains a Chelsea home win recommendation. The injury list is damaging, but Chelsea's overall squad depth and home advantage outweigh a Leeds side that has shown little inclination to win on the road. The 1.85 odds reflect the uncertainty correctly. Confidence is clipped by the five-man absence list.
predictions.value_note: Chelsea 1.85 reflects genuine uncertainty created by their injury list. No value identified — odds are fair.

Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham are carrying genuine momentum after three wins from their last four Premier League outings, and their underlying numbers in the last five games tell a healthy story: xGF 1.48, xGA 0.83, with actual goals overperforming slightly (1.6 scored, 0.6 conceded). The home crowd at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has seen the team beat Crystal Palace and Coventry recently, and with James Maddison, Bergvall, Savio and Udogie all confirmed available, the attacking options are substantial despite the absences of Tel and Mudryk.

Ipswich, by contrast, arrive with the worst xGA in the last five games of any team on this coupon: 2.09. They have conceded 1.8 actual goals per game across that run, and their away record of W1 D1 L3 sits 16th in the division. Gary O'Neil's side were in a battle for survival last season and are navigating a similar path this year. The fully fit squad — O'Neil confirmed all 27 players available — is a positive, but structural defensive fragility is not solved by fitness.

The xG season data for Ipswich is damning: their xGA per game of 1.94 against an xGA-actual of 1.8 suggests they have been neither lucky nor unlucky — they just concede a lot. Their xPts of 11 matches perfectly with their actual 11 points, so there is no regression story to exploit here. What you see is what you get with Ipswich away from home, and what you see is a team that leaks chances.

Tottenham at odds of 1.57 is a touch short for a team with home-record inconsistency (W2 D1 L2 overall at home this season), but the quality gap against this Ipswich outfit, the momentum from UP-FORM flag, and the near-perfect away record of Tottenham recently (wins at Chelsea, draws at Man Utd) make this a confident home win. Ipswich's xGA is simply too porous to survive a fully-loaded Spurs attack on this form.
predictions.value_note: 1.57 is tight but justified given the structural mismatch in xGA between these teams.

predictions.analysis:
Aston Villa's domestic form has been inconsistent — they lost to Bournemouth in the EFL Cup and drew against Fulham at home — but their xGA is improving and the return of Ollie Watkins from injury has stabilised the attack. The home record of W1 D2 L2 is worse than their European performances suggest, and with a Champions League game against a European opponent coming in just three days' time, Unai Emery will be weighing rotation carefully. Missing Cash (concussion), Onana (midfield engine) and Ruggeri is not ideal, but Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi are available alternatives.

What makes this match clearer than the home record suggests is the state of Sunderland. They arrive with a catastrophic injury list that stretches across every line: Brian Brobbey — their top scorer and focal point of everything — is unavailable; Granit Xhaka, the set-piece taker and midfield organiser, is confirmed out with a calf injury; Mundle, Diarra and Ballard are also missing. That is five confirmed absentees for a side that has not won away from home all season (W0 D1 L4), conceding 13 away goals in five games. Their xPts of 15 versus actual 8 points tells of dramatic bad luck or poor conversion, and without Brobbey to threaten, their chance creation collapses further.

The Régis Le Bris quote about being 'fresh and excited' rings hollow when your top scorer, your midfield leader and your first-choice left back are all in the treatment room. Sunderland's beat of Chelsea was a genuine result that showed their attacking quality, but that result came with a fuller squad. Here, they face a Villa side who, despite their European commitments, possess significantly more individual quality at every position.

The Champions League rotation worry is the primary risk. If Emery fields a heavily rotated side, Villa's cutting edge reduces. But even a rotated Villa team should be too strong for a Sunderland side this depleted on the road.
predictions.value_note: Villa 1.82 is fair given rotation concerns. The case for a home win is strong on paper but UCL shadow is real.

predictions.analysis:
Bournemouth are the most in-form team on this entire coupon. Five consecutive wins across all competitions, an xGF of 2.12 and actual GF of 2.6 in the last five games — they are genuinely overperforming their chance creation, suggesting clinical finishing rather than luck. The home fortress at Vitality has seen wins against Leeds, Aston Villa (EFL Cup), Milan (Europa League), Sunderland and Sturm Graz across the last five home outings. That is not a mirage. Marco Rose confirmed all international returnees were healthy, and the structured source confirms no absences for this fixture.

Nottingham Forest, meanwhile, carry the DOWN-FORM flag and a xG story that should alarm any neutral observer. Their xGF of 1.69 in the last five games dwarfs their actual GF of 1.0 — an underperformance of -0.69, the second-largest negative gap on the coupon. At the season level, their xPts of 17 versus actual 9 represents the most dramatic bad-luck story in the division. Oliver Glasner's side is not playing badly — they just cannot score, and their goalkeeper appears to be bailing them out at the other end (xGA 1.10 season, actual 0.9 conceded before this run). That keeper form is fragile, and Bournemouth's relentless press is exactly the kind of opposition that exposes it.

Forest are also travelling with Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez confirmed out, with Schlager and Neco Williams doubtful on the Perplexity report. If Williams — a natural wide defender — misses out, Bournemouth's wide attackers gain space to exploit. The H2H record underlines Bournemouth's dominance: they won 2-0 and 5-0 in the two most recent league meetings at Vitality.

This is one of the clearest-cut matches on the coupon. A fully fit, roaringly in-form Bournemouth at home against a depleted, shot-shy Forest side whose good xG numbers simply are not translating. Bournemouth win.
predictions.value_note: Bournemouth 2.0 offers slight value given the magnitude of their current form advantage.

key_factors: NEW MANAGER: Thomas Frank debuts at Crystal Palace — potential bounce effect, tactical reorganisation
Palace missing Mateta (suspended), Sarr (out), Tomiyasu (out) — gutted attacking options for Frank's debut
Coventry xGF 0.93 but scoring 1.8/g — massive overperformance, regression risk in this match

Coventry's goal-scoring is overperforming xG by the largest margin on the coupon — sustainability is in serious doubt
DROPPED [2]: Palace missing both senior strikers for Frank's first game — insufficient firepower to win away
predictions.analysis:
The dominant narrative here is Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace — a classic new-manager bounce scenario. Frank, who transformed Brentford from a mid-table Championship club into an established Premier League outfit over several years, is precisely the type of appointment that should regenerate energy and belief in a dressing room. His tactical preparation, man-management and ability to quickly implement game-plans are well-documented. The Palace players will be desperate to impress him in his first competitive outing.

However, the bounce logic is complicated severely by an absence list that neuters Palace's most dangerous attacking players. Jean-Philippe Mateta — suspended until 2 December, top scorer and set-piece specialist — will not be available. Ismaïla Sarr is out with a groin injury. Tomiyasu at right-back is also missing. That is both goal threat and delivery from set pieces stripped away simultaneously. Frank will likely reshape his system — possibly to a back three that makes Palace more compact — but without Mateta and Sarr, attacking output is a serious concern against a Coventry side with home advantage.

Coventry are mixed but functional. Their xGF of 0.93 per game is low, yet they are scoring at 1.8 per game — a +0.87 overperformance that is one of the largest on the coupon and must be treated as regression risk. Frank Lampard's side beat Newcastle 4-1 and Sunderland 3-1 at home but lost 0-5 to Brighton and 0-1 to Fulham in the same venue. That inconsistency is real. Missing Wright, Eccles, Woolfenden and Amenda from their squad is a material blow to Lampard's options too.

This is too close to call with confidence. The new-manager bounce is a genuine positive for Palace; the absence of their two best attackers is a genuine negative. Coventry's overperformance in xG makes them a regression risk. The draw at 3.60 is tempting but Palace — even without Mateta — have more quality. I lean very narrowly to Coventry on home advantage, but this is a full-doubles territory match.
predictions.value_note: 1X double at combined odds may offer value — Palace cannot score without Mateta/Sarr but new manager bounce prevents confident away loss.

The case for a home Lincoln win is their structural advantage of being at home in a relegation scrap, with Wrexham missing four or five key offensive players. The case against is Lincoln's own terrible form, particularly at home where they have lost to Birmingham (1-3), Swansea (1-2) and QPR (1-2) in recent weeks. With both teams depleted and Wrexham barely scoring away from home, the draw becomes genuinely attractive at 3.40. Wrexham's creative absence is too severe to back them winning on the road; Lincoln's home form is too poor to back them confidently either. This is the most genuinely uncertain match on the coupon.

Middlesbrough are the dominant home force in the Championship this season. Their home record of W5 D2 L0 — ranking second in the division at home — combined with an xGF of 2.35 and xGA of 0.80 in the last five games describes a team that simply overwhelms opponents at the Riverside. Their shots total of 22.6 per game at home and 7.2 on target are the highest in the Championship, and their xPts of 31 against 29 actual points confirms they are performing almost exactly as their underlying numbers predict. No regression story here — just quality.

The chief concern is Will Lankshear, who has only just returned to group training after a hamstring injury and is doubtful. His contribution — five goals in the season — means his absence reduces Boro's cutting edge. Rokas Pukštas is confirmed out after surgery. Despite these concerns, Kim Hellberg has sufficient attacking depth, and the structured doubts (Jones and Pukštas confirmed) are not crippling.

Bristol City arrive as the DOWN-FORM flag holder, losing three of their last five and carrying an xGF of 1.46 against xGA of 1.82 in that run. Their actual 0.8 GF and 2.0 GA in the last five games tells of a team conceding twice as often as they score. Away from home, however, there is a caveat: their seasonal away record of W3 D3 L1 is surprisingly solid, ranked 8th in the Championship. And the H2H historically has not been kind to Boro — Bristol City have won three of the last four meetings.

The H2H warning is real, but those meetings include Bristol City's home results. At the Riverside, with Boro's home record unbeaten all season, the class difference is too large to bet against. Bristol City's away record was built against different opposition, and Boro's shot volume alone should produce goals. This is a confident home win, one of the clearest singles on the coupon.
predictions.value_note: 1.40 is tight but reflects genuine dominance. The H2H note prevents top-tier confidence.

predictions.analysis:
This is the most tactically fascinating match of the round: two teams level on 29 points, both UP-FORM, potentially separated by this result in the automatic promotion picture. The BBC preview captures it perfectly — both managers know a win here could be decisive for the season narrative. Mark Robins has built Stoke into a compact, defensively disciplined outfit; Chris Davies has Birmingham playing with more adventure and pace around Jay Stansfield.

The xG story here is the most important analytical signal. Stoke's xPts of 18 versus 29 actual points is the largest overperformance of any team on this coupon. They are scoring and winning far more than their underlying metrics predict — an extraordinary gap that almost always corrects over time. Their xGF of 1.05 per game is modest; their actual GF/game is 1.4. They have been clinical to a degree that is statistically unsustainable. Birmingham, by contrast, have xPts of 25 versus 29 actual — a moderate overperformance suggesting genuine quality with modest luck.

Birmingham's attacking numbers are superior in every category: xGF 1.75/g versus Stoke's 1.05/g, shots on target 6.2/g versus 3.4/g, and in the last five games they have been scoring 2.2 goals per game. The concern for Birmingham is August Priske — their top scorer with 6 goals — who is listed as doubtful. If he misses, Birmingham's sharpness in the box is reduced. Stoke at home have conceded only 0.4 goals per game in the last five (xGA 0.87) — the defensive structure under Robins is genuine.

The Stoke overperformance is a severe regression signal. Birmingham are the better team by underlying metrics and should, over time, outperform Stoke. This away win is worth taking at 2.48, with a draw also very much in play. This is not a confident call — it is an analytically informed lean against the public, who back Stoke at 35% — but the xG data is too compelling to ignore.
predictions.value_note: Birmingham 2.48 offers analytical value given Stoke's xG overperformance. This is a contrarian bet against the market.

predictions.analysis:
The context surrounding this match is extraordinary. Vitor Matos has departed as Swansea manager, replaced by an interim panel comprising Ashley Williams, Joe Allen, Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary — four club legends with limited head coaching experience, who have had precisely two training sessions together before this fixture. This is not a standard new-manager bounce scenario; it is an emergency caretaker situation where the squad preparation and tactical coherence will inevitably be disrupted.

Compounding that disruption, Swansea are missing three key players: Marko Stamenic is SUSPENDED for the first game of a three-match ban, robbing them of their CDM and midfield anchor. Gonçalo Franco is out with a hamstring injury for 'a while'. Ronald, their right-winger, is also unavailable despite returning to training. That is two key midfielders and a wide attacker missing for a game requiring a coherent performance. predictions.analysis:
Wolverhampton in the Championship are a team on a different competitive level to Charlton. The xGF of 1.79 per game and xGA of 0.94 over the full season, combined with a home record of W4 D2 L1, reflect a club built to come straight back up from the Premier League. Their UP-FORM flag and six-game unbeaten run going into this match — including wins over Cardiff, Watford and Bristol City — confirm they are building towards a promotion push. The 1.34 odds are very short but reflect a genuine mismatch.

The injury concern is Fer López, their top scorer with 6 goals and 3 assists — the most productive player on any team across the Championship fixtures on this coupon. He is listed as doubtful. If López does not start, Wolves lose their primary creative outlet and goalscoring threat. That would be a meaningful reduction in attacking potency, though Raúl Jiménez and Jordan James are also out already, meaning the attack has already been adapting. Boubacar Traoré and Bellegarde are also doubtful, potentially leaving Wolves' midfield thin.

Charlton, however, make this calculation relatively simple. They have conceded 16 away goals in seven games. Their shots on target of 2.0 per game — the lowest number anywhere on this coupon — reflects a team barely threatening goalkeepers.

Even with López potentially absent, Wolves' home environment, the press facilitated by their corner and shot volumes (7.0 corners per game, 18.2 shots), and Charlton's catastrophic road form makes this one of the clearest results on the coupon. The 1.34 price is justified. Wolves win, almost certainly to nil.
